title: Arbiter engine response envelope
description: Every tool returns this shape: what was checked, what was not and why, and what the engine needs to know next. `meta.schema_version` names the revision; see COMPATIBILITY.md for what may change without moving it.

checked.description: The denominator. Without it, `not_checked: 8` is uninterpretable -- 8 declined out of 47 attempted is a different statement from 8 out of 9.

invariants.description: Evaluations ATTEMPTED. Not declarations, not traversal steps, not matched findings -- all three of which this field has meant somewhere in the past, which is why the two below exist.

steps.description: Traversal steps. Present only for `traverse`, and omitted rather than zero so an absent number is not read as a measured zero.

declared_invariants.description: What the model DECLARES, which is not what the engine evaluates. Present only for `model_describe`.

findings.description: Problems and warnings together. The reasoner splits them by severity, which is a presentation choice; a caller asking what was found wants both.

problem_type.description: `<kind>:<indicator>` for indicator-scoped findings. DOMAIN VOCABULARY -- the part after the colon is the model author's name for the thing, so this is not an enumerable set.

not_checked.description: What was declined, and why. AN EMPTY LIST IS A REAL ANSWER: it means every declared axiom was actually evaluated. This leg is the product -- a clean `findings` beside a populated `not_checked` means nothing was measured, not that nothing is wrong.

reason.description: A CLOSED set, unlike `problem_type`. Read it as three-valued: a member you do not recognise means this engine is newer than your reader, not that the record is malformed.

observations.description: Count INSIDE the window. Present only where it is meaningful.

floor_unreachable_at_this_rate.description: True when the floor CANNOT be met at the observed sampling rate, however long you collect. `remedy` then states the conclusion, because a reader will act on it and should not have to do the arithmetic.

questions.description: What the model is missing, from DISCOVER mode. Empty and absent are different: a caller with no topology supplies none, and `meta.source` says which.

schema_version.description: The ENVELOPE's revision, not the package version. It moves when a reader that worked stops working; adding a key does not move it.

engine_version.description: The version of the installed `arbiter-engine` distribution that produced this envelope, or null when the engine runs from a source tree with no distribution installed. Additive and NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating this key still validates.

source.description: Where the judgment came from: `live` is a real evaluation, `warming_up` is an engine that has not yet seen enough to judge, and `unavailable` means no evaluation happened at all. `unavailable` carries a `reason` and is never an empty success.

forecasts.description: The `forecasts` sub-envelope. Present only on the verb that produces it; NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating it still validates.

shadow.description: The `shadow` sub-envelope. Present only on the verb that produces it; NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating it still validates.

projection.description: The `projection` sub-envelope. Present only on the verb that produces it; NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating it still validates.

entailment.description: The `entailment` sub-envelope. Present only on the verb that produces it; NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating it still validates.

inference.description: The `inference` sub-envelope. Present only on the verb that produces it; NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating it still validates.

discovery.description: The `discovery` sub-envelope. Present only on the verb that produces it; NOT required, so an envelope from an engine predating it still validates.

additionalProperties.description: Tool-specific payloads ride ALONGSIDE the five legs rather than inside them: `model` and `unconsumed_observations` and `unread_threshold_overrides` from model_describe, `evidence` from attest, `unread_properties` from check and gaps, `dropped_declarations` from check -- that last one carried by check because removing a name-derived rule withdrew a check whose cell has no indicator and no axiom to decline on, and a withdrawn check that leaves the envelope identical to a clean pass is the one thing the compatibility policy forbids a patch release from doing. Additive by design -- the four legs plus meta are what every tool satisfies identically, and a tool-specific key is not a change to that contract. `dropped_declarations` carries the values the loader read and did not recognise, so the declaration was not applied: a misspelled axiom name produced an envelope identical to declaring none, and a decline could not express it because `not_checked[].axiom` is a closed enum of the eight names. Same reason as the key beside it, one field further in.

sub_envelope.title: Sub-envelope
sub_envelope.description: ONE DISCIPLINE REPORTING ITS OWN WORK, in the same four-part shape as the envelope above and riding as a payload key beside the legs rather than inside them. A discipline -- forecasts, shadow, projection, entailment, inference, discovery -- does work of a different KIND, and the envelope's own record shape cannot carry it: `not_checked[].axiom` is a closed enum of the eight axiom names and every decline record requires one, so a projection that cannot fit a model would have to invent an axiom to report a refusal. Added because the shape shipped with no schema at all: a downstream reader had nothing to validate against and could only discover the fields by reading the engine's source.

checked.description: THIS DISCIPLINE'S OWN DENOMINATOR, in units it owns -- rules, series, queries, pairs, forecasts. NEVER summed with the top-level `checked.invariants`, which counts axiom evaluations: adding them produces a number that is true of no process. At least one entry is an integer count; non-count entries may sit beside them.

findings.description: What this discipline found. Each finding carries its `evidence`, which top-level findings do not: a discipline's finding is built from a computation the reader did not watch -- a posterior, a breach probability, a lead-lag -- and the numbers behind it are the only way to tell a measurement from an assertion.

not_checked.description: What it refused to judge. `reason` comes from THIS discipline's closed vocabulary and not from `not_checked[].reason` above: the sets are deliberately separate, because `cpt_missing` means nothing to a projector and `filter_not_converged` means nothing to a query planner, and one merged vocabulary would let either accept the other's refusals. Read each as three-valued, the same as the top-level enum: a reason you do not recognise means this engine is newer than your reader.

questions.description: What the discipline needs declared before it can answer.

meta.description: `source` is `live`, `warming_up` or `unavailable`, and a non-live source ALWAYS carries a `reason` -- the envelope's own rule, applied one level down.
